title: Cryptography Based on Radical Divisors in Monoids
content: In this work we introduce a new class of cryptographic primitives based on radical factorizations in monoids and rings. The security of the proposed constructions relies on the difficulty of recovering a radical divisor from a public element, which may contain nilpotent or repeated components masking its structure. We formalize the Radical Divisor Recovery Problem (RDRP), propose encryption and signature schemes based on this problem, and discuss noncommutative and matrix variants in which the asymmetry of division and the presence of nilpotent elements further increase computational hardness. We also present open problems related to the complexity of RDRP.
